tier_reason: The Gazebo maintainers' public benchmark (scpeters/benchmark boxes.cc, results in test_results/BENCHMARK_boxes_model_count.csv and BENCHMARK_boxes_dt.csv) compares Simbody with ODE, Bullet and DART, but states no compiler, flags or CPU model, so it cannot be A; it is an independent measurement but shows no win over ODE or Bullet (only over DART), so it stays at C as a documented not-faster entry.

corrections.workload: Time ratio (wall-clock seconds per simulated second, timeRatio = wallTime / simTime over 10 s of simulated time; lower is faster) in Gazebo-classic: free-floating 1x4x9 boxes, 1 to 101 boxes, with collision off and on; a time-step sweep (0.0001 to 0.001 s, 1 box); plus an object-stacking scene with a large inertia ratio (ROSCon 2014 slide).
corrections.caveats: The README's only performance words are 'high-performance' and O(n) generalized-coordinate dynamics (no numbers), and no reachable benchmark shows Simbody faster than ODE or Bullet; this record documents that it was measured slower or at best equal, so it belongs as a not-faster entry. The measurements come from the Gazebo maintainers' physics benchmark (https://github.com/scpeters/benchmark, Apache-2.0, boxes.cc with GoogleTest and CMake against Gazebo 6; slides pdf/roscon2014_scpeters.pdf and pdf/multibody2015_scpeters.pdf from ROSCon 2014 and ECCOMAS Multibody 2015), results dated about 2014 to 2015 with no CPU model, compiler or flags (the 2015 slides themselves list 'run timing benchmarks on same hardware' as an open item), and the engines run through Gazebo-classic wrappers, so Gazebo overhead is included. Simbody ran with a 0.001 s step and ODE and Bullet with 0.0005 s; the Multibody 2015 slides say this was deliberate ('timestep chosen to give equal accuracy (larger timestep for simbody)', since Simbody takes an extra half-step to estimate error), and the CSV shows the same max position error (0.0245) for all three at those settings. At equal step size Simbody is much slower: in BENCHMARK_boxes_dt.csv (1 box, collision on, complex model, dt 0.0005) Simbody's time ratio is 0.259 vs ODE 0.112 and Bullet 0.129, about 2.3x slower than ODE (derived from page data), though with half the position error (0.01225 vs 0.0245). The 2015 slides summarise accuracy versus computational time as 'comparable'. The stacking slide (real/sim: ODE 0.4, Bullet 0.5, DART 1.1, Simbody >100) gives no explanation or accuracy pairing. Simbody's strengths (O(n) multibody dynamics, accuracy for articulated systems) were not what this speed test targets; the Simbody paper and theory manual were not reachable. The only speed win in this data is over DART, which is not the category baseline.

notes: All numbers in claimed_speedup match the CSV rows (Simbody 1.84/1.87 vs ODE 1.58/1.34, Bullet 1.48/1.44, DART 4.37/7.23 at 101 boxes; 1-box rows and the ROSCon stacking slide also match). Shortcomings to record: not faster than ODE or Bullet (slower from 21 boxes up, about 2.3x slower than ODE at equal step size, roughly equal at equal accuracy), stacking scene over 100x real time vs 0.4 for ODE, no compiler/flags/CPU, 2014-2015 Gazebo-classic wrapper measurements. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, 2.6k stars, 496 forks, not archived, last commit 2026-09-28 (active).
